title: A user survey of an early prototype handheld novel pain measurement device
official: A user survey of an early prototype handheld novel pain measurement device
summary:
Background and study aims
The purpose of this research project is to improve the measurement of pain in healthcare. If pain can be measured better, it may help improve the management of pain.

Who can participate?
Health professionals working in the Rosie Hospital, Cambridge. Healthy antenatal or postnatal women who are inpatients in the Rosie antenatal or postnatal wards and not receiving active care or therapy.

What does the study involve?
An interview survey of opinion of volunteer participants of the value, function and form of a prototype pain measurement device which participants will be encouraged to handle and use. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
There are no direct personal benefits of participating. There should be no expected risks from participation.

Where is the study run from?
Cambridge University Hospitals (Rosie Hospital)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
October 2026 to March 2027. 

Who is funding the study?
Obstetric Anaesthetists' Association

Who is the main contact?
Dr Jim Bamber, Consultant anaesthetist, james.bamber1@nhs.net
conditions: Opinions of health professionals and patients about the design and function of an early prototype device for pain measurement

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Any health professional who is working in the local centre and whose job role is likely to involve pain assessment of patients as judged by the investigator will be invited to participate in the survey
2. Healthy women who are inpatient in the local centre on the antenatal and postnatal wards and who are not  receiving active care or therapy at the time of the invitation for inclusion
3. English speaking
Exclusion criteria:
1. Health professionals whose work would not be expected to involve patient pain assessment and those to decline the invitation to participate
2.	Patients who are unwell or receiving active ongoing treatment
3.	Patients who have a disability or condition that will preclude or inhibit their ability or to cause any discomfort to use the prototype device
4.	Women who cannot understand, read or speak English
5.	Women who are in distress of any kind or who are in pain
6.	Women who are not inpatients on the antenatal or postnatal ward
